newsitem.title: INDIA: Two killed, 7 wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: Two killed, 7 wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.

text.p: Two girls were killed and seven other people wounded when separatist guerrillas hurled a grenade at a crowded market near Srinagar, police said on Wednesday.
They said the attack occurred late on Tuesday at a security picket in Pulwama town, 30 km (19 miles) south of Srinagar, summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state.
The grenade missed the security forces and exploded on the road, a police spokesman said.
"Two girls, Sahmeeda and Shameema, succumbed to injuries," a police statement said.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting for independence or merger of Kashmir with neighbouring Pakistan. Jammu and Kashmir is mainly Hindu India's only majority state.

More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990 when discontent against Indian rule erupted into revolt. India accuses Pakistan of training and arming Kashmir's Moslem militants, a charge denied by Islamabad.
